body:
## Summary

Please add 32-bit ARM targets to `--python-platform` (e.g. `armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf` and `armv7l-manylinux_2_xx`), alongside the existing `aarch64-manylinux_2_xx` / `x86_64-manylinux_2_xx` ones.

## Use case

We build a linux/arm/v7 (Raspberry Pi) Docker image from a `uv.lock` that pulls several packages from piwheels on armv7l:

```toml
[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "piwheels"
url = "https://www.piwheels.org/simple"
explicit = true

[tool.uv.sources]
psutil = { index = "piwheels", marker = "platform_machine == 'armv7l'" }
```

piwheels moved some files to a new host, so a URL pinned in `uv.lock` started returning 404. The lock still looked valid (`uv lock --check` passes), and the arm/v7 image build failed at `uv sync --frozen`. The fix was `uv lock --refresh-package psutil`.

We'd like CI on x86_64 to catch this without QEMU, by running a real download and hash check for the target:

```
uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-install-project --no-build --python-platform armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf
```

That already works for arm64 and amd64 (`--python-platform aarch64-manylinux_2_36`, etc.), but there's no armv7 value, so the architecture most likely to hit this (the one depending on piwheels) can't be checked.

## Notes

- uv already treats armv7 as a supported platform (uv binaries and managed Python downloads for `armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf`), so this seems to be only a missing entry in the target list.
- piwheels wheels are tagged `linux_armv7l`, not manylinux. The existing Linux targets already accept plain `linux_<arch>` wheels (checked with `aarch64-manylinux_2_36` and a `py3-none-linux_aarch64` wheel), so the same behaviour for armv7 would cover piwheels.
- Possibly related: #18127 (`platform_machine` markers evaluated against the host rather than the target). For this to be useful, `platform_machine` should evaluate to `armv7l` for the new target so the piwheels sources above are selected.
title: Support 32-bit ARM (armv7) targets in `--python-platform`
